proposals.exact_quote: I don't believe that either part of our mandate is generally at war with the other part. I do not believe that price stability and full employment is an either-or proposition. There have been policymakers over the last several generations who have thought that there is a strict tradeoff there. That isn't my judgment.
proposals.financial_importance: This statement rejects the traditional Phillips Curve framework, signaling that the Fed under Warsh's leadership will not reflexively tighten policy or suppress employment solely on the assumption that a strong labor market inherently drives inflation.
proposals.editorial_takeaway: Fed Chair rejects strict tradeoff between price stability and full employment.
proposals.why_it_matters: By distancing himself from generations of policymakers who believed in a strict dual-mandate tradeoff, Warsh signals a highly flexible reaction function. This philosophy suggests the Fed may tolerate tighter labor markets for longer, fundamentally altering how market participants model interest rate paths during economic expansions.
proposals.material_qualifiers: The speaker uses the qualifier "generally" ("not generally at war"), leaving open the possibility that exceptional macroeconomic circumstances could still force a tactical tradeoff between inflation and employment.
